data.name: Agripina
data.gender_notes: Agripina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'agri', meaning 'fair' or 'handsome', and 'pina', meaning 'pine tree'. Agripina was the name of several prominent Roman women in early Christianity, including the wife of Emperor Claudius II and the mother of Emperor Nero. The name Agripina carries the meaning “Fair, Lovely” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Agripina usually hope their child will grow to embody fair, lovely and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Agripina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fair, Lovely.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Agripina total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Agripina is a name of Roman origin, which carries the legacy of an influential civilization that left its mark on European history. Naming a child Agripina connects them to a rich cultural heritage and an enduring sense of history. The name evokes images of Roman grandeur, power, and resilience.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Agripina is associated with the martyrdom of St. Agripina, who is said to have been beheaded in Sicily during the persecution of Christians by Emperor Hadrian. This link to martyrdom adds a deeper layer of spiritual meaning to the name. Believers may see Agripina as a reminder of the courage and faith of early Christians, and a symbol of enduring devotion to God in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Agripina, derived from Agrippina, means "little field" or "little vineyard" in Latin. In a Christian context, it represents the nurturing and growth of the soul, symbolizing one's dedication to cultivating spiritual richness and bearing fruit for God.

biblical_reference.note: Not a direct biblical name, but derived from Greek words used in the New Testament.

name_in_real_life.story: Hannah Agripina, a minister in Dublin, Ireland, shares that their name Agripina meaning "Fair, Lovely" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
